text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hosni Mubarak follows operations to relieve the damage caused by floods in Assiut, Aswan and the Red Sea and asks for provision of all needed food and aid.
- Mubarak tells journalists that for him to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu there must be implementation of the Hebron agreement.
- Greek President Costis Stephanopoulos will visit Egypt in the second half of December.
- Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says that Israel's door to the Arab world is through the peace process, not through economic conferences.
- Economically viable quantities of gold found by Australian company in the eastern desert.
- Ethiopia to decide by Wednesday on court death sentence against three men for trying to assassinate Mubarak.
- Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro to visit Egypt on November 29 for a two day visit to include important political talks with Mubarak on the peace process.
- Military planes transport aid and equipment to flood-hit areas in the south and bring tourists to Cairo.
- The United Nations started its talks on Boutros Boutros-Ghali's return as secretary general for a second term. He has support from all over the world - except from the United States.
- Mubarak in his interviews with European journalists urges all parties to rescue peace.
